children: Indonesia's GDP growth could moderate to 5.1% in 2H from 5.45% in 1H, mainly due to slower domestic consumption growth and a larger drag from net exports, RHB economist Wong Xian Yong says in a note. He keeps his 2026 GDP growth estimate at 5.2%, with investment expected to remain the main support as household spending cools. Strong investment in manufacturing, infrastructure and downstream industries should partly offset weaker consumption and external trade. Net exports are expected to keep dragging as imports of capital goods and raw materials outpace subdued exports. Government spending should continue to support domestic demand, although its growth contribution is expected to ease. Wong maintains his 2026 inflation forecast at 2.8%, with upside risks from higher food and energy prices toward year-end and into early 2027.(yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
